subject: Oceanography
title: Coastal Deposition
description: A fast breakdown of Coastal Deposition for builders.

hook.text: Not all coasts are eroding—some are growing, as waves and currents deposit sand in sheltered areas.

buildup.text: Deposition occurs where wave energy drops—behind headlands, in bays, and where currents slow.

discovery.text: Spits form when longshore drift carries sand past a coastline bend into open water.

twist.text: Tombolos connect islands to the mainland with sand ridges—built by waves refracting around the island.

climax.text: Coastal deposition builds new land—but it's always temporary, reworked by the next big storm.

punchline.text: The sea builds land with one wave and takes it with the next.

quiz.question: What is a spit?
options: A sand deposit extending past a coastline bend into open water
